checks.finding: Every architectural/technology decision in design.md carries an explicit, citation-grounded rationale. Examples: the union-match multi-component rule (Design Decisions 'Multi-affected-component trigger/when matching rule') cites investigation.md INV-012 (evaluate-predicate's single-component CLI shape) and the identical soundness argument Epic A4's own INV-019 already establishes; the 'facet-name aggregation, predicate-instance keyed' rule (B7) cites Epic A2's own schema silence at specs/epic-190-a2-capability-registry/requirements.md:169-173; the journaled 'staged generation, single atomic commit' publication mechanism cites Epic A1's already-Passed design.md:927-1016 as the reused protocol shape (adversarial finding B1); the .yaml-over-.json choice for resolver-evidence.yaml cites Epic A4's own REQ-007 placement rationale verbatim (Data Plan). No inline 'we will use X' statement was found without an accompanying because/since-style justification or citation.

design.md's 'Open Questions' section (restating requirements.md Open Questions) carries OQ-001 and OQ-002 in prose, without the literal 'Blocks Implementation: yes/no' / 'Resolution Path:' field labels the check calls for. However each names a plausible owner (OQ-001: 'a future caller's own contract'; OQ-002: 'a future epic (plausibly A6/A8)', investigation.md OQ-002) and each is explicitly framed as non-blocking to this Phase-1, contract-fixing package's own scope (requirements.md Non-goals: 'this package fixes the contract only'; design.md Open Questions: 'Neither blocks this Phase 1 package's own infrastructure surface', mirrored in infra-spec.md Open Questions). Per reviewer-calibration.md's severity guidance, a non-blocking open question with a stated (if informally worded) owner is an acceptable Minor completeness note, not a Major finding. OQ-003 -- the one question that could plausibly have blocked REQ-007's own caller-insertion-point claim -- is explicitly resolved in this revision with a concrete SKILL.md:60 file:line anchor plus a two-signal drift check (design.md Design Decisions 'caller insertion point'/'anchor fingerprint', M6).

No performance requirements found in requirements.md. This feature is a deterministic, single-invocation CLI/script family with no runtime service (security-spec.md Service Level Objectives: 'N/A -- no live service to hold an availability/latency SLO'; infra-spec.md Scaling Strategy: 'no runtime service, no concurrency model of its own'). REQ-005's own 'byte-identical output' / dual-runtime-parity requirement is a correctness/determinism property, not a numeric throughput/latency/concurrency SLA, and is separately verified via the parity test suite (TEST-022/023).
